main_text.head: FLOS VI.
Subditis novæ Rerumpublicarum mutationes fugiendæ.
main_text.p: Tales sunt hominum mores, & talia ingenia: ut semper præsentia fastidiant imperia, quantumvis mitia & bona: novosque dominos & nova imperia expetant. Quoniam enim nulla tam felix est gubernatio, quin habeat aliquid difficultatum: ideo fit, ut leviter presfi[?] à præsentibus gubernatoribus subditi, his excussis quærant novos. Sed quas Rerumpublicarum mutationes plerumque fieri in deterius, populi ISRAELITICI satis superque docet historia: cuius politia omnibus mundi regnis antecellebat: DEO ipso in medio populi versante, & in gravioribus causis responsa inter Cherubim edente, judices quoque & duces belli pios & probos, quotiescunque rogabatur, eligente. Verùm qui præ-senti gubernationis forma, quà DEO ejusque verbo subjiciebatur: pertæsus[?] à SAMUELE, (qui huc usque 2881.aheneus ipsi fuerat murus & propugnaculum, & quem constabat regi atque conservari divinitus, cujus quoque innocentiæ & justitiæ in gubernatione postea in publicis regni comitiis, in Gilgalis celebratis, apertum & ingenuum perhibuit testimonium) ad circumfusa-rum gentium morem petiit sibi dari Regem: lubri-cum homuncionis[?], in horas mutari soliti, imperium immutabilis DEI præferens dominationi & gubernationi. 1.Reg.8.

Quanta verò malorum lerna sub hac populi Israelitici postulatione latuerit: & quàm prochivis sit virium in violentiam lapsus, & quàm præceps regni in tyrannidem mutatio: sub Saulis & aliorum nonnullorum Regum imperio, malo suo didicit. Utique enim imperiorum mutationes non fiunt sine magnis calamitatibus, tâ publicis quàm privatis: ut verissimè dixit Xenophon:

page.notes: Running head and page number taken from the top of the scan; the page number is hard to read and marked [?]. The margin numbers 2881 and 2882 are placed as notes beside the lines where they stand; the second one (2882) is at "publicis regni" in the text and the note was placed at the start of the first line of that passage, so its exact line is approximate. The Greek line of Xenophon is partly visible but could not be read letter by letter, so it is marked illegible. The word after "pertæsus" and the word "homuncionis" are doubtful. The "1.Reg.8." reference is italic and at the end of the paragraph.
